title: Density of a finite Gaussian product
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set, let $c=(c_i)_{i\in I}$ be a real vector, and let $v\ge0$ with $v\ne0$. The product of the Gaussian measures with means $c_i$ and variance $v$ has, relative to Lebesgue measure on $\bbr^I$, density $z\mapsto\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$, where $p_v(c_i,z_i)$ is the scalar Gaussian density with mean $c_i$ and variance $v$.
replaced: Let $I$ be a finite set, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v>0$, and $\mu_{c,v}=\bigotimes_{i\in I}N(c_i,v)$. The measure $\mu_{c,v}$ has Lebesgue density $z\mapsto\prod_i p_v(c_i,z_i)$, where $p_v(c_i,z_i)$ is the scalar Gaussian density.
